idiom_name: static Rule table: function-pointer conditions + actions over a Fact struct
implementation_notes: In plain C the pattern is a data structure plus a loop: an array of rules, each holding a predicate function pointer over a context struct (the working memory) and an action function pointer, evaluated in a bounded pass. Nothing is parsed or reflected at run time, so rules are compiled in - the 'rules change more often than the code' motivation only materialises if the table is loaded from a config file whose condition/action names resolve to registered functions. Keep predicates side-effect free, let only actions mutate the fact, and mark a rule fired after it runs so a mutating action cannot re-trigger it.
pitfalls: The table is compiled in: without a loader mapping rule names to registered functions, changing one rule means changing C source, and there is no reflection to look the function up.

A rule whose action writes a field its own condition reads matches again on the next pass - CLIPS-style engines suppress this with refraction; here the 'fired' flag or a cycle bound must do it explicitly.
Function pointers carry no fact type: wiring a condition to the wrong struct, or leaving an action NULL, compiles cleanly and fails at run time - assert the invariants when the table is loaded.

variants.name: Embedded CLIPS production rule system
variants.idiom_name: embedded CLIPS: defrule / deftemplate + fact-list + agenda
variants.implementation_notes: CLIPS (C Language Integrated Production System, developed at NASA's Johnson Space Center) is the classic way to get a real production rule system into a C program: rules are written in CLIPS syntax, facts are asserted into a fact-list, and the inference engine decides which rules fire, ordering activations on the agenda by salience and using refraction to stop a rule from re-firing on unchanged facts. It is written in C and embeddable, so the host program asserts facts and reads results while the policy lives in a rule file that can be edited without recompiling the host. Choose it when matching spans many facts (Rete) and modules/salience are needed; stay with the hand-written table when three conditions suffice.
variants.code_sketch:
(deftemplate order (slot units) (slot loyalty) (slot discount))
(defrule volume-discount "bulk order"
   ?f <- (order (units ?u&:(> ?u 100)) (loyalty ?l&:(> ?l 2)))
   =>
   (modify ?f (discount 0.10)))
(assert (order (units 250) (loyalty 5) (discount 0.0)))
(run)
pitfalls: You now ship an interpreter and a second language: rules sit outside the C type system, so a slot or function typo is a parse/run-time error instead of a compiler diagnostic.

Facts are untyped templates in a global fact-list: two modules asserting the same deftemplate interact, and truth maintenance (modify/retract) is the only thing stopping a rule from re-firing - asserting a fact your own rule matches loops.
